sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- lens_diagnostics: lens_diagnostics source=session reads the session cache and an empty cache is not proof of a clean file; use source=lsp scope=paths for changed files when cached findings are absent or stale
- symbol_search: Find files by identifier
- effective_config: Explain resolved configuration
- project_report: Orient in a project before choosing a file
- module_report: Outline a source module before reading a body
- read_symbol: Read one symbol's body instead of the whole file
- read_enclosing: Read the enclosing symbol or callback body for a line
- pi_lens_activate_tools: Activate a situational tool
- subagent_gate: Run subagent tasks with bounded retries and a required success quorum
- workspace_session_summaries: Inspect same-CWD session summaries before potentially overlapping repository work
- subagent: Delegate focused work to child agents; compose multi-child work in one workflow call.
- subagents_enable: pi-subagents is installed. For authorized specialist, independent-review, or parallel work, call subagents_enable, then subagent. Authorization must come from the current request or applicable instructions; complexity alone is not authorization.
- ask_user_question: Ask the user up to 4 structured questions (2-4 options each) when requirements are ambiguous
- workflow: Delegate substantive independent or staged work to subagents with a JavaScript workflow, optionally composing agent calls with parallel(), pipeline(), or both
- workflow_control: Inspect and manage workflow runs directly by canonical run ID.

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use subagent_gate instead of raw subagent calls when a delegated result must be retried safely or a success quorum must be enforced.
- Set each subagent_gate task retrySafety to read-only only when rerunning it cannot duplicate file mutations or external side effects; omission defaults to may-write.
- Use workspace_session_summaries when another Pi session in the same working directory may overlap the current work.
- After workspace_session_summaries, compare goals, files or symbols, decisions, and next steps; when overlap is material or ownership is unclear, coordinate through intercom before writing.
- Use ask_user_question whenever the user's request is underspecified and you cannot proceed without concrete decisions — you can ask up to 4 questions per invocation.
- Each question MUST have 2-4 options. Every option requires a concise label (1-5 words) and a description explaining what the choice means or its trade-offs. The user can additionally type a custom answer via the automatically appended "Type something." row on every question, or press Esc to abandon the questionnaire. Do NOT author "Other" or "Type something." labels yourself — reserved labels are rejected at runtime.
- Set multiSelect: true when multiple answers are valid. Provide an options[].preview markdown string when an option benefits from richer side-by-side context (mockups, code snippets, diagrams, configs) — single-select only. The "Type something." row is appended to every question; in preview mode it expands to the full pane width while typing so the custom answer is not cramped into the narrow options column. If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option and append "(Recommended)" to its label.
- Do not stack multiple ask_user_question calls back-to-back — group all clarifying questions into one invocation.
- The `workflow` tool runs multi-agent orchestration — it fans decomposable work out across subagents, and fits tasks shaped like: repo-wide inspection, independent parallel research/checks, multi-perspective review, or fan-out/fan-in synthesis. ONLY call it when the user explicitly opts in — via the workflow trigger word, `/workflows run`, or their own words (e.g. 'run a workflow', 'fan this out', '并行审一遍'). For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit — do not call it; you may briefly offer it (with a rough cost) as an option instead.
- Use workflow_control for workflow lifecycle management; do not ask the user to type /workflows when this tool can perform the action.
- Use stop to terminate or quit a run. Closing the navigator does not stop a run.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.description: Run a JavaScript workflow that delegates work to subagents with agent(), optionally composing calls with parallel() and pipeline().

Add phases: [{ title: 'Phase' }] only when the workflow has named phases, and declare only phases it will use. With multiple phases, call phase('Exact Title') before each phase's work or set `phase` in the agent options. Use `await workflow(savedName, childArgs)` to run a saved workflow inline; nesting is limited to one level and shares the parent run's concurrency, agent, and token limits. Optional quality helpers include verify(), judgePanel(), loopUntilDry(), and completenessCheck(). Optional control helpers include retry() and gate(); budget exposes total, spent(), and remaining(), and phase('Name', { budget: N }) sets a phase token limit. The optional `agentType` option selects a named user or project definition that can bind tools, a model, and role instructions; use it only when its name and purpose are provided in context. Its bound model overrides `tier`; an explicit `model` overrides both. Use plain JavaScript only; imports, require(), filesystem modules, Date.now(), Math.random(), and new Date() are unavailable. Use phase('Name'), agent(prompt, opts), parallel(arrayOfFunctions), pipeline(items, ...stages), log(message), args, cwd, process.cwd(), and budget. The workflow must call agent() at least once. parallel() requires functions, not promises, and returns results in input order: await parallel(items.map(item => () => agent(...))). pipeline(items, ...stages) runs stages sequentially for each item while items proceed concurrently; each stage receives (previousValue, originalItem, index).

# Implementation Plan: Image (UI-example) questions for the question-me skill

Task folder: `docs/tasks/ef13c0e6-273e-4ce2-8227-7e730db77fb5/`
Source request: give the question-me skill an image-question option — agent proposes up to 4 detailed UI/logo
descriptions, the survey renders them as generated example images, the human picks one, and the chosen image is
saved in the task folder and referenced from SURVEY.md (or equivalent). API key lives in general settings;
skill config gets an image-gen dropdown (`none` removes the image-gen section entirely, otherwise select a
provider). First provider: Muse/Meta image generation, designed for later extension. Key stays server-side.
Plan scope: planning only — no code is changed in this stage.

## Goal & scope guard

- A new survey question type for image choice. The agent writes up to 4 detailed descriptions; the **backend**
  generates the images (gateway model — runners/agents never see the key), stores them in the task folder
  `assets/` directory, and the survey UI renders them as a single-pick image question with a descriptions
  fallback when generation is unavailable or fails.
- General (system) settings gains a persisted per-provider API-key store with a new Settings UI section.
- The question-me skill config gains an `imageGen` keyword (`none` | provider id) rendered as a dropdown in
  the workflow editor's Skills panel; `none` removes the image-gen section from the agent prompt entirely.
- Non-goals for this slice: more than one real provider (Muse Image only, behind a registry built for more);
  per-project keys (shared key only, per q2 default); multiple sizes (one fixed size, per q6 default);
  video/edit/reference-composition features of Muse Image; changing existing `single`/`multiple` behaviour
  (byte-identical when `imageGen: none`, which is the default).

## Inputs and survey position

- Grill survey (`SURVEY.md`) is present but `answers` is `{}` — Round 1 (q1–q7) is **unanswered**. Every survey
  answer below is a provisional default (the options marked Recommended, or the task text where it decides),
  not a user decision. Re-confirm q1 (provider identity) before locking Phase B.
- The prior report named in the stage brief (`idea-20261102-005723.md`) is **not present** in this checkout;
  only `SURVEY.md` exists in the task folder, so no prior findings could be reused beyond the survey itself.

### Survey factored in — provisional defaults (reversible)

| # | Survey question | Provisional decision | Rationale & how it shapes the plan |
|---|-----------------|----------------------|-------------------------------------|
| q1 | Which image service first (Muse/Meta)? | **Muse Image (`muse-image-1.0`) via the Meta Model API** (`https://api.meta.ai/v1`), API-key auth | Matches the task text ("muse/meta image gen interface"); verified to exist as a developer API in Aug 2026 (see Sources). Exact request schema is pinned in Phase 0 spike; a provider interface + mock provider means no other work blocks on it. If the user names a different service, only the provider adapter changes. |
| q2 | Where is the image key saved? | **One shared key in general settings** | The Recommended option and the task text agree. Implemented as a new persisted system-level secret store (none exists today — see finding 5) with an env override. |
| q3 | How do image choices work? | **Up to 4 pictures, pick one favourite** | The Recommended option. New question `type: "image"` behaves like `single` (one selection) with image cards instead of radio rows. |
| q4 | When are pictures created? | **Most reliable: eagerly at park time, in the background** | The Recommended option ("no preference — most reliable") plus the task's reliability steer. Backend starts generation when the task parks for survey; images are ready (or failed-with-fallback) before the human opens the page. Survey GET reports per-image status so the UI can show progress if generation is still running. |
| q5 | Pictures cannot be made? | **Show the written descriptions instead** | The Recommended option. Descriptions are always in the round JSON (the agent writes them), so fallback is free: render option text + a notice, never block answering. |
| q6 | Picture shapes in v1? | **One fixed size** | The Recommended option. One configured size (square-ish default TBD in Phase 0) for all image questions; no per-question size field in v1. |
| q7 | How many picture questions per survey? | **Several allowed, each up to 4 pictures** | The Recommended option, with a cost guard: a per-survey image cap (default 12 = 3 full questions) enforced by the backend; questions beyond the cap render descriptions-only with a notice. |

## Research findings (verified in this checkout — big pieces first)

1. **Survey model — `shared/survey.js` (~500+ lines; verified).** Single source of truth shared by backend and
   frontend: `QUESTION_TYPES = ["single", "multiple"]`, `normalizeQuestion`, `validateSurvey`, `serializeRound`,
   `applyAnswers`, `unansweredRequired`, `surveyStatus`. Any new question type must extend normalize + validate +
   serialize together or rounds will fail validation on write (`appendSurveyRound` / `saveSurveyAnswers` reject

   notes: string }` subsets of options.
2. **Survey backend — `api/work/taskSurvey.js` (verified) + routes in `api/work/taskWorkRoutes.js`.**

3. **Task image storage + serving already exists — `api/routes/taskImages.js` + `api/work/taskAssets.js`

   (`![alt](assets/<name>)`); helpers cover allowlist (`png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp`), `sanitizeImageName`,

4. **Skill config pipeline (verified end-to-end).** `skills/question-me/KB_config.json` declares

   `stage.skills[i].config` and layer over defaults in `resolveSkillKeywordMap` (`api/skills/skillInjection.js`);

   per-stage keyword values in `frontend/src/components/workflow/StageSkillsPanel.jsx` (~1020 lines): kbRef

   free-text/JSON — so a metadata-driven provider dropdown follows an existing pattern (Phase A2).
5. **No persisted system-level secret store exists (verified by grep).** System Settings
   (`frontend/src/components/settings/SystemSettingsContent.jsx` + `settingsTabs.js`) has persisted tabs
   (Storage/Notifications/Prompt Layout via their own endpoints) and wireframe tabs (Models/Engine: "changes
   here are not saved yet"). Global config is env-driven and **read-only** (`api/config/schema.js`, served
   redacted via `GET /status/config` with `secret: true` flags). Per-project settings persist through the
   project store (`PATCH /projects/:id`). So "save an API key in general settings" requires a **new**
   system-secret store + endpoints + UI section — this is the biggest new-backend piece (Phase A3).
6. **Survey UI — `frontend/src/components/tasks/SurveyPage.jsx` (577 lines; verified).** Renders rounds via a
   `QuestionField` component (radio/checkbox + Notes), `showIf` visibility via shared helpers, Save vs
   Submit-and-advance, `Save answers`/`Submit & continue`/`Continue without questions` buttons. Image questions

   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_JOIN_TOKEN` in `api/config/schema.js`) and operate on task docs; the task explicitly says
   the key must stay in the backend. Decision: **backend gateway** — the runner/agent only writes descriptions
   into SURVEY.md like any other question text; all provider calls happen server-side. This is also the easiest
   option: no runner protocol change, no credential distribution, works for embedded runs identically.
8. **Provider grounding.** Muse Image is Meta Superintelligence Labs' image model, served to developers as
   `muse-image-1.0` on the Meta Model API (`https://api.meta.ai/v1`, API-key auth, ~$0.01/image announced) and
   alternatively via fal.ai (`meta/muse-image/text-to-image`). Exact REST schema/auth headers must be verified

## Approach — make change easy, then make the change

> Workers before jobs: first create the seams (conditional skill sections, metadata-driven keyword dropdowns,
> provider registry + mock, persisted key store, survey-model image support), each shippable and tested on its
> own with zero behaviour change; then wire the feature through them. Research and the riskiest backend piece
> (secret store + provider contract) come first so later UI work cannot discover a structural blocker.

Key decisions:

- **Backend gateway, not runner generation.** Easiest (no runner protocol/credential work) and most reliable
  (one code path for embedded + Runner runs; key never leaves the server; retries/timeouts centralised).
- **Eager background generation at park time.** `parkTaskForSurvey` parks synchronously as today, then
  fire-and-forget `ensureSurveyImages()` generates missing images, writes them via `taskAssets` helpers, and
  splices `images[]` status into the round JSON. Survey GET surfaces per-image `ready/pending/failed` so the
  UI can poll or fall back. Rejected alternative: lazy generation on first survey GET — simpler code, but the
  human waits on image latency and refresh races are harder; rejected alternative 2: synchronous at park —
  blocks stage finish on provider latency and risks timeouts.
- **Descriptions are the durable contract; images are derived artifacts.** The agent writes
  `type: "image"` + ≤4 description `options`; the backend fills `images[]`; answers stay `{ selected, notes }`
  selecting by description string, so every existing validation/completion path keeps working and q5 fallback
  is automatic.
- **Chosen image persistence:** on successful submit/advance, the backend copies the selected image to a stable
  name (`assets/survey-r<round>-<qid>-chosen.png`) and appends a `## Chosen designs` markdown section to the
  survey file with `![...](assets/...)` references — satisfying "saved as an image in the task folder with a
  reference in SURVEY.md or equivalent" without disturbing the append-only round JSON.

## Step-by-step workflow (ordered: big/research early)

### Phase 0 — Research spike & contract freeze (blocks everything; no prod code)

1. Verify the Muse Image developer API against Meta's current docs (endpoint, auth header, text-to-image
   schema, sizes, response bytes/URL, rate limits, pricing). Record the exact pinned contract + doc URL in
   this file's Sources section. If the Meta Model API is unreachable from the test environment, record fal.ai
   as the verified fallback path (do not implement it in this slice).
2. Freeze the round-JSON contract for image questions (proposed; confirm or amend here before Phase A):

   images: [{ option: <index>, file: "assets/<name>", status: "pending|ready|failed", error?: string }] }`.

3. Freeze the `imageGen` keyword contract: KB_config default `"none"`; stage override `"none"` or a provider
   id from the registry (`"muse"` in v1); unknown values fail safe to `none` + process-log warning.
4. Freeze the conditional-section syntax for SKILL.md (proposal: `{{#if imageGen}} … {{/if}}` blocks evaluated
   against the layered keyword map, where `"none"`/`""`/missing is falsy). Confirm it composes with the
   existing unknown-`{{...}}`-preserved guarantee.
5. Re-confirm q1 (Muse Image vs another service) and the per-survey image cap with the user if reachable;
   otherwise proceed on the provisional defaults above.
6. Exit: contract written here; spike code (if any) thrown away or kept only as the mock provider fixture.

### Phase A — Make the change easy (seams; each independently testable, no behaviour change)

- **A1. Conditional skill sections.** Extend `api/skills/skillInjection.js` with the Phase-0 conditional syntax
  (render/omit blocks from the layered keyword map), keeping byte-identical output for skills without
  conditionals (guarded by the existing `promptCuration.skills.contract` tests). Unit tests: truthy/falsy/
  missing/`none` keyword, nested unknowns preserved, size-cap accounting unchanged.
- **A2. Metadata-driven keyword dropdowns.** Extend `StageSkillsPanel.jsx` so a KB_config keyword entry with
  UI metadata renders a `<select>` instead of free text. Proposed metadata:
  `{ "value": "none", "description": "…", "ui": "provider-select", "providerApi": "/api/image-gen/providers" }`,
  options fetched from the backend registry (id + label), with static `enum: [...]` as the offline fallback.
  Unit tests with a mock client; existing free-text/JSON paths untouched.
- **A3. Provider registry + key store (biggest backend piece).** New `api/imageGen/` module:

  - `keyStore.js`: per-provider keys in a `0600` JSON file under the KainBain dir (`api/kainbainDir.js`

  - Routes: `GET /api/image-gen/providers` (id/label/configured only — never keys), `PUT`/`DELETE`

- **A4. Survey-model image support.** Extend `shared/survey.js`: accept `type: "image"` in

---
name: question-me
description: Generate a set of survey questions up‑front for an agent stage, write them to `{{outputFile}}` in the task folder, and flag the stage as awaiting human input. The skill is used to replace iterative “grill‑me” interactions with a single questionnaire.
lastUpdated: 2026-10-29
---

# Question‑Me (Survey Generator)

Use this skill when you want an **agent stage** to produce a list of multiple‑choice questions (with an optional free‑form notes field) for a human to answer later. The skill:

1. **Generates questions** based on the stage’s prompt.
2. **Writes** a `{{outputFile}}` file in the current task’s directory (`docs/tasks/<taskId>/`).
3. **Never overwrites** existing content – it reads the file first and **appends** a new round of questions at the bottom, preserving any prior answers.
4. **Marks the stage as awaiting human input** (task status `waiting_human`) so the UI shows the survey banner and the survey page.
5. Supports **conditional questions** via one simple `showIf` object form: `{ "questionId": "q1", "value": "Option A" }` or `{ "questionId": "q1", "values": ["A", "B"] }`. The UI hides those questions unless the condition is met. No other condition syntax is supported — never write string expressions.
6. **Question ids must be unique across the whole survey** (including every appended round). Re-using an id makes answers ambiguous, so append rounds with fresh ids such as `q5`, `q6`.

## Expected `{{outputFile}}` format

The file contains a **machine‑parseable JSON block** wrapped in a fenced code block (`survey-json`). The JSON is the single source of truth; a human‑readable markdown preview is generated from it by the UI.

```markdown
# Survey – generated by the "question‑me" skill

```survey-json
{
  "round": 1,
  "generatedAt": "2026-10-29T13:00:00.000Z",
  "stage": "{{stageId}}",
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "q1",
      "type": "single",
      "text": "What is the primary security concern?",
      "options": ["Authentication", "Authorization", "Data protection", "Other"],
      "required": true,
      "showIf": null
    },
    {
      "id": "q2",
      "type": "multiple",
      "text": "Which regulatory frameworks apply?",
      "options": ["PCI‑DSS", "HIPAA", "GDPR", "None"],
      "required": false,
      "showIf": { "questionId": "q1", "value": "Data protection" }
    }
  ],
  "answers": {
    "q1": { "selected": ["Data protection"], "notes": "PII in uploads" }
  }
}
```

*The UI renders each question as a set of radio‑buttons or check‑boxes with a **Notes** textarea underneath. Fill `generatedAt` with the current UTC time in ISO‑8601 (as above) and `stage` with the stage id already resolved into this prompt (`{{stageId}}`) — never leave a placeholder token in the written file; the backend validates the round and rejects unreadable ones.*

When the user finishes the survey, the UI updates the `answers` object in‑place (preserving the surrounding JSON) and saves the file.

### Append‑only behaviour
- If `{{outputFile}}` already exists, the skill **reads** it, determines the next `round` number, and **appends** a new JSON block under a new heading `## Round N`.
- Existing `answers` objects are left untouched.
- The skill must never delete or rewrite previous rounds.
{{#if imageGen}}
## Image questions (generated design examples)

This stage may also ask **image questions**: the human sees up to 4 generated pictures (UI mocks, logos, …) and picks one favourite. Image generation for this stage runs through the configured provider (`{{imageGen}}`); the backend generates the pictures after you write the survey — you only write detailed descriptions.

Write an image question like this:

```survey-json
{
  "id": "q3",
  "type": "image",
  "text": "Which dashboard design should we build?",
  "options": [
    "Dark analytics dashboard, left sidebar navigation, teal accent charts, dense data table, modern SaaS look",
    "Light minimal dashboard, top navigation bar, large KPI cards, generous whitespace, friendly rounded corners"
  ],
  "required": true,
  "showIf": null
}
```

Rules:
- `type` is exactly `"image"`; `options` holds 1–4 detailed descriptions (each one becomes a picture — write them detailed enough to render a UI mock or logo: layout, palette, key elements, style).
- Answers work like `single`: the human picks one favourite description; the chosen picture is saved into the task folder (`assets/`) and referenced from `{{outputFile}}` for downstream stages to work from.
- Never write an `images` field yourself — the backend owns it (generation status per picture). If generation is unavailable, the survey falls back to showing your descriptions as options, so always make them self-explanatory.
{{/if}}
## How the engine treats the skill
- During stage execution, after the agent returns **success**, the backend inspects the stage’s skill list. If `question-me` is present, it reads `{{outputFile}}` and decides:
  - **Unanswered required questions** (or no `{{outputFile}}` at all) → the task parks with status `waiting_human` instead of auto‑advancing. The task detail page shows the survey banner; the survey page opens at `/tasks/:taskId/survey`.
  - **Explicitly empty round** (`questions: []` — you had good reason to ask nothing) → the run advances normally, no parking.
  - **Already answered** → the run advances normally.
- Submitting the survey (`POST /tasks/:taskId/survey`) merges answers only — questions are never added, removed, or renamed there. A partial save stays parked; a complete submit advances the task to its next stage, which may then read `{{outputFile}}`.

## Downstream stages
Tell the stage after the survey (e.g. the plan stage) to factor in `{{outputFile}}` — for example: "Factor in {{outputFile}} into your plan. If there is not enough information, fail the stage with information needed." A failback re-runs the question stage, which appends a fresh round at the bottom.

## Human‑only edge‑cases
- If you genuinely have **no questions**, still write one round with `questions: []` rather than writing no file. An empty round advances without parking; a missing file parks so a human confirms there is nothing to ask (the survey page offers Continue in both cases).

## UI considerations (mobile & desktop)
- Render each question inside a `<fieldset>`.
- Options are full‑width touch targets; use `type="radio"` for `single` and `type="checkbox"` for `multiple`.
- The **Notes** textarea is optional but always present; on mobile it expands to the full width.
- Conditional visibility is evaluated client‑side; hidden questions are collapsed but their stored answers remain unchanged.
- Accessibility: all inputs have `aria‑label` and are keyboard‑navigable.

## Configuring the output file

The output file name is read from the skill configuration. In `KB_config.json`:

```json
{
  "keywords": {
    "outputFile": { "value": "SURVEY.md" },
    "minQuestions": { "value": "0" }
  },
  "defaults": { "mode": "direct" }
}
```

A stage attachment can override the file name without editing the skill, for
example:

```json
{ "name": "question-me", "config": { "outputFile": "FEEDBACK.md" } }
```

Accepted config keys (canonical first, then aliases): `outputFile`, `surveyFile`,
`surveyFileName`, `fileName`, `targetFile`, `file`. Plain names without an
extension become a `.md` file (`FEEDBACK` → `FEEDBACK.md`); anything else must
already end in `.md`. Path traversal or unsafe names fall back to `SURVEY.md`.

Multi-stage tasks should give each question stage its own file, e.g.
`FEEDBACK.md`, `SECURITY_QUESTIONARY.md`, `INTENT_SURVEY.md`, while the
default single-survey setup keeps `SURVEY.md`.

## Suggested minimum question count

`minQuestions` is a soft prompt hint only; the engine never enforces it. A value
of `0` disables the suggestion.

## Minimal `KB_config.json`
The skill defaults to `SURVEY.md` and a disabled minimum, so an empty object is
still sufficient (`{}`).
